# Building SQL Equivalence Proofs from Query Rewrite Rules

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#equitrace)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2610.30100v1) · arXiv:2610.30100v1, 21 October 2026

**Reading coverage:** All six PDF pages: Sections 1-6, Figures 1-3, Tables 1-4 and references. Figures 2-3 and Tables 1-3 visually checked. No appended supplement in this version.

## Research question

Determine SQL equivalence while exposing the transformations and schema assumptions that justify a positive decision.

## Method

EquiTrace aligns Calcite logical plans, applies bounded rewrite searches, and records two derivations to a common witness. Replay uses the original rule implementations; semantic validity of admitted rules is a separate trust assumption.

## Evaluation

Tests 3,233 query pairs across Text-to-SQL-derived, curated and LLM-rewrite corpora. Proof rates use expected-equivalent subsets; execution agreement supplies many labels. QED and SQLSolver comparisons share the rewrite corpus.

## What the results support

Reports 648/1,106 proofs on Text-to-SQL pairs and 97/240 on execution-identical LLM rewrites. Join alignment matters disproportionately; broad join regions, outer joins and windows remain difficult.

## Limits and qualifications

UNKNOWN is not inequivalence. Calcite-derived tests favor the rewrite vocabulary. The abstract cites 1,242 analyzed proofs, while Section 5.1 describes 764; their relationship is unexplained, so neither is used as an unqualified analysis count.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Useful for reference-SQL evaluation, conditional on trusted rules and schema constraints; it cannot verify that a reference captures user intent.
